question: Do the seven frozen B component models make sufficiently different per-target hit errors to justify equal-rank aggregation, and does the existing combined_equal_rank model dilute the stronger component outcomes?

frozen_methods.primary: Compute the 21 pairwise Pearson correlations of per-target main-number hit counts across the seven component models only; report mean, median, minimum, and maximum without selecting or dropping components.
frozen_methods.secondary: Compare combined_equal_rank mean hits with each of the seven component means and with their unweighted mean.

random_reference.use: descriptive reference only; do not promote a component based on this historical screen

exclusions: No three-line portfolio claim or STRICT_PASS_READY promotion.
No parameter search, model tuning, threshold relaxation, alpha change, block-length change, or comparator change.
No component promotion from same-sample historical results.
interpretation_limit: Hit-count correlation is error dependence, not ticket-number overlap. This study is a historical B single-ticket diagnostic and cannot qualify target-1251 three-line purchase readiness.
preregistration_hashing: The preregistration is committed before reading or calculating the E061 outcome statistics.
